description: The human-rights and legal pressure track - a channel barely covered in the original source documents
verification_status: confirmed by a primary source (Business & Human Rights Resource Centre, data as of 22 July 2026)

bhrc_2021_2025_data.trend: rising every year; peaked at 148 allegations in 2025
bhrc_2021_2025_data.concentration: 10 Chinese companies account for 65% of all allegations
bhrc_2021_2025_data.nature_of_allegations: impacts on livelihoods, health, land rights, workplace deaths, water pollution; in 2023-2025, 18 people were attacked for raising these issues
bhrc_2021_2025_data.geography: Indonesia has the highest case count; Africa saw the sharpest 2025 increase (+122% versus 2024, 100 allegations)
bhrc_2021_2025_data.corporate_response_rate: low response rate to inquiries; having a human-rights policy (both Zijin and Huayou do) does not correlate with practice
bhrc_2021_2025_data.source: BHRC, 'Shifting ground: Human rights, Chinese investment and the rush for transition minerals', July 2026

us_cbp_wro.content: a US Customs and Border Protection Withhold Release Order against copper and copper products from Serbia Zijin Copper D.O.O., Zijin Mining's Serbian subsidiary
us_cbp_wro.significance: a precedent: a US sanctions tool applied to a Chinese mining group via its third-country subsidiary

pressure_on_financiers.content: the US House Select Committee on China (chaired by Rep. Moolenaar) sought answers from Morgan Stanley in November 2025 over its underwriting of Zijin Gold International's IPO; Zijin Mining has been added to the UFLPA Entity List
pressure_on_financiers.significance: pressure is shifting from the companies themselves to the banks that give them access to international capital

situation_in_the_drc.forced_labor: per the 2024 US Department of Labor report, more than three-quarters of artisanal miners may be working under conditions with indicators of forced labor; estimates put the number of children at cobalt mines at at least 25,000
situation_in_the_drc.2023_dol_report: the TFM (CMOC) and Deziwa (CNMC) operations were named with documented violations in the report (the user's original document cites over 251 cases - not independently re-verified)
situation_in_the_drc.private_security: AFREWATCH (May 2025) published a separate report on PSCs and human rights in Haut-Katanga and Lualaba; from March 2025, video footage circulated of clashes between Chinese company managers and Congolese workers and artisanal miners
situation_in_the_drc.pollution: scientific studies document heavy metals in the air, soil, and water around Kolwezi; per rights groups (RAID), Zijin ignores inquiries, while CMOC and Glencore engage at least partially

why_this_is_leverage: Unlike market competition, where subsidized dumping makes head-on rivalry pointless, the human-rights and sanctions track hits the link that Chinese state-bank credit cannot replace: access for Chinese groups to Western sales markets and capital.
